title: Xuanwu Hospital implants Epilcure, a responsive neurostimulator, in a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy on March 9, 2022
summary: Xuanwu Hospital implanted Epilcure in March 2022. Later methods describe threshold-triggered stimulation; a learned seizure predictor and this patient’s benefit remain unestablished.
account: On 9 March 2022 a team at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, implanted the Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system. Hospital president Zhao Guoguang and neurosurgeon Shan Yongzhi led it. The patient, a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, was the first enrollee in a hospital-led NMPA registration clinical trial. Sources: cnBeta and Kuai Keji (12 March 2022), both citing the neurosurgery department's WeChat account. The reports describe an AI chip implanted in the skull, with intracranial electrodes monitoring electroencephalography (EEG) rhythms around the clock. The reports say that the device predicts an imminent seizure and delivers an interfering rhythm to block seizure formation at the focus. Bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy is called a relative contraindication for open surgery. The operation went smoothly and the stimulator's indicators worked normally during surgery. Post-operative reconstruction showed precise electrode placement and clear EEG signals (cnBeta). The initial accounts give no seizure outcome, patient age or follow-up for this patient. A later clinical-team paper identifies the maker as Hangzhou Genlight MedTech and describes five clinician-configured detection algorithms that trigger stimulation when signal measures cross set thresholds. That paper does not establish that a learned model predicted seizures or link an individual seizure outcome to this first implantation.
purpose: Epilcure was built to detect the onset of seizures from continuously monitored intracranial EEG and deliver stimulation to abort them in people with drug-resistant epilepsy. Implanting it for that purpose was the intended use, though no seizure outcome is yet reported.
system: Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system (brain-computer interface)
developer: Hangzhou Genlight MedTech Co. Ltd. (GenLight MedTech), identified in the later clinical-team publication.
deployer: Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing
segment: Implanted neuromodulation device in a registration clinical trial
taxonomy_note: The documented outcome is a successful implantation with the device working, not seizure reduction.

ratings.reason: The reports establish a successful implantation with the stimulator working normally and electrodes precisely placed. No reduction in seizures, follow-up or patient-reported outcome is given, so the benefit to the patient's health is not yet established.

ai_role.statement: The hospital announcement described AI-assisted EEG monitoring and automatic stimulation. The later clinical paper describes five clinician-configured signal-detection algorithms and threshold-triggered stimulation, so it does not establish that a learned model predicted seizures.

fields.account: On 9 March 2022 a team at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, implanted the Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system. Hospital president Zhao Guoguang and neurosurgeon Shan Yongzhi led it. The patient, a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, was the first enrollee in a hospital-led NMPA registration clinical trial. Sources: cnBeta and Kuai Keji (12 March 2022), both citing the neurosurgery department's WeChat account. The reports describe an AI chip implanted in the skull, with intracranial electrodes monitoring electroencephalography (EEG) rhythms around the clock. The reports say that the device predicts an imminent seizure and delivers an interfering rhythm to block seizure formation at the focus. Bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy is called a relative contraindication for open surgery. The operation went smoothly and the stimulator's indicators worked normally during surgery. Post-operative reconstruction showed precise electrode placement and clear EEG signals (cnBeta). The initial accounts give no seizure outcome, patient age or follow-up for this patient. A later clinical-team paper identifies the maker as Hangzhou Genlight MedTech and describes five clinician-configured detection algorithms that trigger stimulation when signal measures cross set thresholds. That paper does not establish that a learned model predicted seizures or link an individual seizure outcome to this first implantation.

fields.title: Xuanwu Hospital implants Epilcure, a responsive neurostimulator, in a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy on March 9, 2022
fields.headline: Xuanwu Hospital implants China's first responsive neurostimulator

provenance.basis: Preserved from the existing AIBD record; external sources were not rechecked.
Deterministic content version assigned by the local migration.

fields.account: On 9 March 2022 a team at Xuanwu Hospital, Capital Medical University, Beijing, implanted the Epilcure closed-loop responsive neurostimulation system. Hospital president Zhao Guoguang and neurosurgeon Shan Yongzhi led it. The patient, a man with drug-resistant bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy, was the first enrollee in a hospital-led NMPA registration clinical trial. Sources: cnBeta and Kuai Keji (12 March 2022), both citing the neurosurgery department's WeChat account. The reports describe an AI chip implanted in the skull, with intracranial electrodes monitoring electroencephalography (EEG) rhythms around the clock. The reports say that the device predicts an imminent seizure and delivers an interfering rhythm to block seizure formation at the focus. Bilateral temporal lobe epilepsy is called a relative contraindication for open surgery. The operation went smoothly and the stimulator's indicators worked normally during surgery. Post-operative reconstruction showed precise electrode placement and clear EEG signals (cnBeta). The initial accounts give no seizure outcome, patient age or follow-up for this patient. A later clinical-team paper identifies the maker as Hangzhou Genlight MedTech and describes five clinician-configured detection algorithms that trigger stimulation when signal measures cross set thresholds. That paper does not establish that a learned model predicted seizures or link an individual seizure outcome to this first implantation.

produced_by: Intracranial electrodes at the epileptic focus feeding continuous EEG to a chip implanted in the skull
Clinician-configured EEG detection algorithms that trigger stimulation when signal measures cross set thresholds, as described in the later clinical paper
Enrollment in the hospital-led NMPA registration trial for patients whose epilepsy is drug-resistant and unsuited to open surgery
must_hold: Electrode placement is precise and signals are clear, as the post-operative reconstruction reported here
Detection and stimulation settings must be appropriate for the patient; a seizure outcome for this first implantation is not established by the inspected sources
